title: Feature: download a calendar file of everything coming up
body:
### What it should do
In the Calendar tab, planners tap **Download for my calendar** and get one .ics file with their event days, key dates, payments due, venue bookings, blocked days, rentals out and back, and teammate shifts. It opens in Google Calendar, Apple Calendar and Outlook. A live link that updates on its own needs a server, so say "live calendar link: coming soon" under the button.

### Who uses it
Planners and venues

### Where in the app
Planner portal → Calendar tab

### Done when
- [ ] The button downloads a valid .ics file built from plCalItems()
- [ ] Each item becomes an all-day event (or timed when it has a time), with the who line as its description
- [ ] Importing the file in Google Calendar shows the items on the right days
- [ ] Works on a phone-sized screen
- [ ] Help desk entry added (js/16-planner-portal.js)
- [ ] A check added to agents/regressions.json
- [ ] `bash agents/check_all.sh` passes

### Notes for the builder
Build the file in the browser from `plCalItems()` (js/16-planner-portal.js) and use the existing `download()` helper. Escape commas, semicolons and new lines as the iCalendar format requires. No new data, no rule change.

_From the Host Mode To-Do List. Start the builder by adding the `claude` label._

title: Feature: one-of-a-kind keepsake art for each event
body:
### What it should do
The keepsake page shows a piece of generated art made just for this event: shapes and colors drawn from the event's theme colors, with a pattern seeded by the event code and the honorees' names, so every event's art is different and the same event always gets the same art. Hosts can download it as an image.

### Who uses it
Hosts and guests

### Where in the app
The keepsake page (keepsakeView in js/06-event-types.js)

### Done when
- [ ] The art uses the event's five theme colors
- [ ] The same event always draws the same art; two different events look different
- [ ] A Download button saves it as a PNG
- [ ] Looks good in light and dark themes
- [ ] Works on a phone-sized screen
- [ ] Help desk entry added (js/16-planner-portal.js)
- [ ] A check added to agents/regressions.json
- [ ] `bash agents/check_all.sh` passes

### Notes for the builder
Draw on a canvas or SVG with a small seeded random function (no Math.random, so it repeats). Keep it gentle and elegant, not busy. This touches a guest-facing screen, so run `python agents/compare_screens.py before` and `after` and mention the result in the pull request.

_From the Host Mode To-Do List. Start the builder by adding the `claude` label._

title: Feature: thank-you cards guests get after the party
body:
### What it should do
After the event, the host writes one thank-you note in the host console, and every guest sees a pretty thank-you card on their phone the next time they open the event link: the event's colors, the honorees' names, the host's note and a link to the photo album and keepsake. Hosts can also download the card as an image to text or post.

### Who uses it
Hosts and guests

### Where in the app
Host console (js/04-moderator.js) and the guest home screen (js/03-guest.js)

### Done when
- [ ] The host can write, change and turn off the thank-you note
- [ ] Guests see the card only after the host turns it on
- [ ] Spanish for every guest-facing word (see the spanish-check Skill)
- [ ] The card can be downloaded as an image
- [ ] Works on a phone-sized screen
- [ ] Help desk entry added (js/16-planner-portal.js)
- [ ] A check added to agents/regressions.json
- [ ] `bash agents/check_all.sh` passes

### Notes for the builder
Store the note under the event (an `ER()` path) next to similar host settings, and check database.rules.json already lets the host write there; if it needs a rule change, stop and say so (Phase 1 builders don't change rules). Guest-facing: run the before/after screen comparison.

_From the Host Mode To-Do List. Start the builder by adding the `claude` label._

title: Feature: guest needs on the guest list (allergies, accessibility, seating)
body:
### What it should do
Each guest on an event's guest list can have needs: food allergies or diet, accessibility (wheelchair, hearing, seating near an exit), and a seating note. Moderators and hosts add them on the guest list, and the guest list importer picks them up from a column like "Allergies" or "Dietary".

### Who uses it
Hosts, planners and moderators

### Where in the app
The guest list in js/11-tonight.js and the importer in js/14-client-portals.js

### Done when
- [ ] Needs can be added and edited for each guest
- [ ] The importer recognizes allergy, diet, accessibility and seating columns, with duplicate checks and undo like the other kinds
- [ ] Guests with needs show a small marker and a count at the top ("6 guests with needs")
- [ ] Spanish for any guest-facing words
- [ ] Works on a phone-sized screen
- [ ] Help desk entry added (js/16-planner-portal.js)
- [ ] A check added to agents/regressions.json
- [ ] `bash agents/check_all.sh` passes

### Notes for the builder
Part 1 of 2. Part 2 puts these on the event sheet and the caterer's vendor page. Follow CLAUDE.md's importer pattern. Guest names stay off anything public.

_From the Host Mode To-Do List. Start the builder by adding the `claude` label._

title: Feature: floor plan, part 1 of 4: draw a space and place tables
body:
### What it should do
In the planner portal, planners pick a venue space, set its size, and drag in round and long tables, chairs, a stage, a dance floor, a buffet, a bar and decor, drawn to scale. They can move, turn, copy and delete pieces, and save several layouts per event.

### Who uses it
Planners, venues and decorators

### Where in the app
Planner portal: a new Floor plans tab, following CLAUDE.md's "How planner portal features are built"

### Done when
- [ ] Pieces snap to a grid and are drawn to scale
- [ ] Works with a finger on a phone and a mouse on a computer
- [ ] Layouts save live and load again
- [ ] Demo layout added to the planner demo (raise PDEMO_V)
- [ ] Layouts are added to Download everything
- [ ] Works on a phone-sized screen
- [ ] Help desk entry added (js/16-planner-portal.js)
- [ ] A check added to agents/regressions.json
- [ ] `bash agents/check_all.sh` passes

### Notes for the builder
The biggest feature on the list: keep part 1 to drawing and saving only. Use SVG so it stays sharp. Parts 2 to 4: seating and inventory, a 3D view, sharing with clients.

_From the Host Mode To-Do List. Start the builder by adding the `claude` label._

title: Feature: practice copy of Host Mode for testing risky changes
body:
### What it should do
A separate practice copy of the app and its own database, so agents and Roy can try risky changes (rules, security, guest screens) without touching real events.

### Who uses it
Roy and the agents

### Where in the app
A second Firebase project plus a way to point the app at it (for example a ?practice=1 switch)

### Done when
- [ ] Roy has made the second Firebase project (free plan)
- [ ] The app can be opened against the practice database
- [ ] The practice database has the same rules
- [ ] Agents' checks can run against it

### Notes for the builder
Needs Roy to create the Firebase project first. Back-end builder (Phase 2).

_From the Host Mode To-Do List. Roy needs to decide or do something before a builder starts._

title: Feature: automatic tests for the database rules
body:
### What it should do
Every pull request that changes database.rules.json runs tests in GitHub with Firebase's free testing tool, checking who can read and write each important path (planners, clients, teammates, vendors, staff, the public).

### Who uses it
Roy and the agents

### Where in the app
.github/workflows and a new agents/rules_test file

### Done when
- [ ] Tests cover each path in the rules
- [ ] A rule change that opens private data to the public fails the check
- [ ] Runs on pull requests that change the rules

### Notes for the builder
Back-end builder (Phase 2). No secrets needed: the testing tool runs locally inside GitHub.

_From the Host Mode To-Do List. Start the builder by adding the `claude` label._
